question: Can a small weave program preserve declared crossing alternation across odd-sized tile seams before a Godot renderer is trusted?
production_path: baseline: use pinned GA Godot plan and VC-005 asset-cleanup lesson to define a proposed scene boundary, without claiming an import
model: use global crossing IDs and an over-under parity rule on a 3-by-3 base tile repeated to 6 by 6
experiment: execute a synthetic evaluator for global parity and restarted tile parity, count adjacent relation violations
counterargument: a labeled 2D grid and ordinary JSON manifest may be clearer and cheaper than a 3D weave or a new DSL
falsifier: reject a 3D educational candidate if an ID binding is wrong, a seam breaks alternation, or task comprehension falls below a fixed 2D baseline
hypothesis: A global-coordinate crossing rule can expose odd-tile seam errors that local tile checks miss, but this alone cannot validate a Godot scene or justify a new DSL.
evidence: At Demerzel commit f23ccae6c049d9066a1be2221c68f3b0bcf48373, the synthetic fixture and evaluator define both variants and an exact adjacency checker; one 6-by-6 evaluation produced 36 unique IDs per variant, 0 global-parity violations, and 12 restarted-tile violations.
The pinned GA Godot integration plan at dc2e74cbd992a298f67efb928b5b3754615e1924 is a proposal, not an import receipt. No renderer, learner trial, or human review is measured by this research cycle.

Five answered exercises include invented future click, viewer, and frame-time outcomes. The executable fixture is the only measured artifact. Research duration was not instrumented, so duration_seconds=0.
